checklist.item: Secrets and server texts (tokens, header values, SMTP or upstream replies, file contents) in errors, logs and responses
checklist.evidence: 25 hostile `pulse init --yes --setup full <dir> ...` runs with a marker in check URL user info, query and path, unknown --check keys, bad host, id and timeout, webhook and status URL user info and query, a console URL path, --smtp-user, --smtp-password-env, a stray positional and --src-dir: each exits 2 and names only the flag, the position (`--check #1`) and the rule. Marker hits: 0, except an unknown option name echoed as a plain word, the --dir path, and the path of a stray positional URL (note N1). DOCKER_HOST=tcp://u:<marker>@127.0.0.1:1 with `pulse status`: exit 3, `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at tcp://127.0.0.1:1`; encoded passwords and https user info give `(hidden)`; a raw `/` in the password is passed on (finding 4). A bad .env line holding the marker and a YAML error in compose.override.yaml: `failed to read .../.env: line 7: key cannot contain a space`, `yaml: line 3: did not find expected ',' or ']'`, no marker. secrets-init with a spaced or placeholder token: rule only, 0 hits; a 3 GiB input: `secrets-init: unexpected Error ENOMEM`. Running full stack started by the CLI: `docker compose logs` (12 lines) and `docker inspect` Env, Cmd and Labels of 6 containers have 0 hits of the admin token, probe token and console key; `pulse status` shows none; `pulse up` prints only the /readyz status code (cli/ready.ts:75). e2e/redact.test.sh 54 cases passed. Defects: findings 2 and 3 (raw stack trace with minified source, no file content), finding 4, note N2.

checklist.item: Authentication before any other check; status codes and their order on admin routes
checklist.evidence: pulse-deploy serves no HTTP route of its own; the admin routes belong to pulse-api and pulse-console. Deploy-side reachability from `docker compose config --format json`: minimal api 127.0.0.1:3000; full console 127.0.0.1:8082, status *:8080; demo console, mailpit and status on 127.0.0.1; dev api and console on 127.0.0.1, status *:8080; the CLI-rendered minimal, demo and full match. Running full stack: api PortBindings {}, console 127.0.0.1:18082. The CLI project guard refused 4 bypass attempts with exit 1 before any destructive Compose call (same project name in a second directory, a volume renamed to another project's, an external volume, `export COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=` in .env); DOCKER_HOST in .env is ignored by Compose; the 6 volumes of the stack stayed intact.

checklist.item: Body and size limits on every method, also before any write
checklist.evidence: demo/targets.mjs is the only HTTP server in a setup (demo only, not published) and never reads a body: POST /up with 100 MiB gives 200, RSS 32,768 kB before and 36,608 kB after; GET /../etc/passwd and /up?x=1 give 404. Test-only receivers (e2e/hook.mjs, cli/test/hook-receiver.ts) not reviewed. secrets-init reads and checks every input before its first write (scripts/secrets-init.mjs:161); a 3 GiB input fails with one line and writes nothing. The CLI reads pulse.json, .env, notify.json, token and key files whole without a size cap: a 5 GiB sparse secrets/console-secret-key drives `pulse init --force` to a 5.0 GiB peak RSS and an uncaught ENOMEM before any write (finding 3); a FIFO there is refused. A 600 KB notify.json nested 100,000 deep crashes `pulse up` before `docker compose up` (finding 2).

checklist.item: Input validation at every trust boundary; validators never throw on any input type
checklist.evidence: Fuzz: 21 exported validators and parsers x 23 values (483 calls; undefined, null, NaN, BigInt, symbol, function, objects, a getter object, a revoked proxy, empty, 1 MB, NUL, CRLF, lone surrogates, URL variants, 200,000-deep JSON text, __proto__ JSON, a 20-digit number). String inputs: 0 unexpected throws; every refusal is a UsageError (exit 2). TypeErrors only for non-string values, which cannot be reached because argv, prompt lines, file text and Docker output are strings. A --status-url with `${AUDIT_ENV_SECRET}$HOME`, a double quote and a backslash is written single-quoted to .env; `docker compose config` with the variable set gives `https://h.example/$${AUDIT_ENV_SECRET}$$HOME/a"b\c` (literal); cli/yaml.ts:26 doubles `$` in every user string. secrets-init refuses PULSE_PROBE_LOCATIONS=../<marker>; PULSE_LOCATION is not checked (note N3). Defect: the notify.json walker of the env preflight throws RangeError on deep nesting and runUp re-throws it (finding 2).

checklist.item: No accessor or getter of untrusted input runs
checklist.evidence: The CLI gets untrusted data only as strings (argv, prompt lines, environment, Docker stdout and stderr, file text) or JSON.parse output (pulse.json, notify.json, docker compose config and ps JSON, volume labels); neither can hold an accessor. pulse.json and Docker JSON are read through Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(...).value (cli/docker.ts:174, cli/init.ts:119). The fuzz passed a getter object to all 21 functions: getterCalls=0. secrets-init reads only file text and environment strings.

checklist.item: SSRF: allowed targets, environment lookups, redirects (cross-origin, https to http), forwarded headers
checklist.evidence: The CLI sends no HTTP request itself; every Docker call is an argument array with stdin /dev/null (cli/docker.ts:53). The only in-container request is fetch("http://127.0.0.1:<port>/readyz"), port from pulse.json accepted only as an integer 1 to 65535 (cli/docker.ts:186); service names match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62} and cannot become an exec flag. scripts/bump-images.sh: registry fixed to https://ghcr.io (line 11), never from the environment; curl without -L (no hit for ` -L` in bump-images.sh), so no redirect is followed and the pull token is not forwarded; tag and service checked (17 test cases passed). wait-ready.sh accepts a mailpit address only if it matches ^127\.0\.0\.1:[0-9]+$ (line 84). COMPOSE_* is removed from the child environment and refused in .env; DOCKER_HOST in .env has no effect. No setup sets a trust-proxy or forwarded-header option (grep: no hit). Services reach the api at http://api:3000 on the Compose network (common/services.yaml:21, 30, 40, 49); redirect handling on that hop belongs to the service audits (security-status-2026-11-06-2).

CLI: temp name in the target's directory with wx (O_EXCL) and the final mode, then rename (cli/write-install.ts:280). 11 planted cases with --force: symlinked config/, helpers/, secrets/, .env, compose.yaml, .pulse-init.lock, secrets/probe-token-default, an unused secrets/probe-token-old and .pulse-backup, and a 0755 secrets/: each exit 1 (`is a symlink; pulse init never writes through a link`, `another pulse init is running`, `.pulse-backup/: is not a directory`, `mode 0755 is wider than 0700`). A hard link at config/api/checks.json is replaced by the rename and backed up; the linked file keeps its content. Modes: .env 0600, secrets/ 0700, tokens 0600. secrets-init: temp file and rename, 0400, 1000:1000 (scripts/secrets-init.mjs:76); in the running stack `-r-------- 1000 1000` for every secret file, /run/pulse and /config read-only (`touch: /run/pulse/x: Read-only file system`); 66 secrets-init test cases passed. init-secrets.sh: mktemp and mv -n (7 cases passed). bump-images.sh: mktemp and mv. No fsync anywhere, and demo/init.mjs rewrites the demo checks file in place (note N4).

checklist.item: Dependencies, Docker base images and CI actions pinned and approved (`docs/approved-packages.md`)
checklist.evidence: common/services.yaml: five pulse images 0.1.0@sha256, oven/bun:1.4.0-alpine@sha256:07235578..., alpine/openssl@sha256:1c361a20..., axllent/mailpit:v1.32.0@sha256:0790692b..., equal to approved-packages.md lines 56 to 58; scripts/check-setup.sh: all rules passed, exit 0. No runtime dependency (compiled, private). Dev dependencies exact and approved: @biomejs/biome 2.6.3, lefthook 2.2.2, @types/node 26.6.6, @types/bun 1.4.0, typescript7 (npm:typescript@7.0.2), pulse-config by full SHA. bun.lock: 155 entries, 155 sha512 hashes. bun audit: 1 moderate, minimatch@10.2.6, dev only via eslint in pulse-config (note N5). Actions: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 (v7.0.1) with persist-credentials: false at every use, oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 (v2.2.0), pulse-config check.yml by SHA; permissions: contents: read at the top of both workflows; no pull_request_target; no event data in run lines. bun pm untrusted blocks only pulse-config's prepare; lefthook postinstall and the root prepare run, the root prepare also under CI=true, while the release build job holds a contents: write token (finding 1).

findings.title: The release build job exposes a contents: write token to bun install (root prepare runs lefthook) and to the compile step
findings.command: Read release.yml:38-53 (job build: permissions contents: write, job-level env GH_TOKEN, bun install --frozen-lockfile, bun build); in a copy: rm .git/hooks/pre-commit; CI=true bun install --frozen-lockfile --force; ls .git/hooks | grep -v sample; bun pm untrusted
findings.excerpt: release.yml:41 `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` (job env, permissions contents: write at :38-39); :51 `- run: bun install --frozen-lockfile`. Copy: `118 packages installed` then `pre-commit` recreated by the root prepare `lefthook install` (package.json:17) under CI=true. bun pm untrusted: only `@lorenzh/pulse-config ... [prepare]` blocked; lefthook postinstall runs.
findings.impact: Every install-time script and native binary of a dev dependency, and the compile step, run with a token that can create tags, edit releases and upload assets. A compromised dev dependency could swap the CLI release binaries before publish computes SHA256SUMS, so the checksums would match the swapped binary. Exact pins with sha512 integrity keep the risk low.
findings.fixDirection: Set GH_TOKEN only on the upload step (and in create and publish), not at job level in build, and run bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts in the release jobs.

findings.title: A deeply nested config/notify/notify.json makes pulse up crash with an uncaught RangeError and a dump of minified source
findings.command: pulse init --yes --setup full <fresh dir> (project auditdeep); replace config/notify/notify.json with one channel nested 100,000 objects deep (600,031 bytes); pulse up --dir <install>. Also envPreflight called directly at depths 1,000 to 50,000.
findings.excerpt: 6,064 bytes on stderr: two lines of minified CLI source, then `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.` / `at r (/$bunfs/root/pulse:530:2293)` (repeated) / `at async br (/$bunfs/root/pulse:547:30)` / `Bun v1.4.0 (Linux x64)`. Containers created: 0. Direct calls: depth 20,000 ok, 50,000 RangeError.
findings.impact: A broken or hostile notify.json makes pulse up fail with a dump of bundled source instead of one error line naming the file and the rule. Nothing starts and no secret is shown.
findings.fixDirection: Walk the channels iteratively or with a depth limit that refuses deeper input as a CommandError naming the file; add a catch-all in cli/main.ts that prints one line (error name and code) and exits 1, as scripts/secrets-init.mjs:275 does. That also covers finding 3.

findings.title: pulse init --force reads secrets/console-secret-key whole, without a size check, outside the error handling
findings.command: pulse init --yes --setup full <install>; replace secrets/console-secret-key with a 5 GiB sparse file (mode 0600); pulse init --yes --setup full --force <install>, RSS sampled every 0.1 s
findings.excerpt: peak_rss_kb=5278592; stderr: `ENOMEM: not enough memory, read 'big1/secrets/console-secret-key'` / `at Ks (/$bunfs/root/pulse:535:1779)` ... plus minified source lines. A FIFO at the same path: `pulse init: secrets/console-secret-key: is not a regular file`. secrets-init with a 3 GiB input: `secrets-init: unexpected Error ENOMEM`.
findings.impact: An oversized key file in the install directory makes pulse init allocate its full size and crash with a stack trace before any write.
findings.fixDirection: Refuse a key or token file larger than a few hundred bytes before reading it (keyRefusals at :158, preflight called at :346), and rely on the catch-all of finding 2.

findings.title: maskUserInfo masks only up to the first /, ?, # or space and needs // after the scheme, so a malformed DOCKER_HOST is passed on
findings.command: DOCKER_HOST=<tcp URL whose unencoded password holds a "/"> pulse status --dir <install>; unit run of maskUserInfo over 14 line shapes
findings.excerpt: `pulse status: cannot reach the Docker daemon: Failed to initialize: unable to resolve docker endpoint: parse "tcp://u:pa/<marker>@127.0.0.1:1": invalid port ":pa" after host` (marker shown); `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at tcp://127.0.0.1:1/<marker>`. Unit run: 6 of 14 shapes keep the marker (raw /, #, ? or space in the password, `https:u:p@h`, `token=` text). A well-formed `tcp://u:<marker>@...` gives `(hidden)`.
findings.impact: Part of a malformed credential in the operator's own DOCKER_HOST reaches stderr. Docker prints the same text when it is called directly.
findings.fixDirection: Mask from the scheme to the last @ before whitespace or a quote, not only up to the first /, ? or #.

notes.text: shown() keeps the path of an http(s) URL: `pulse init --yes --setup full <dir> https://hooks.example/services/T0/B0/<marker>` gives `pulse: unexpected argument https://hooks.example/services/T0/B0/<marker>; see pulse init --help` (exit 2). By design, but webhook URLs often hold their secret in the path. It shows only for a stray positional.

--webhook-url, fragment included, is stored in config/notify/notify.json with mode 0644 (stat: 644). The interactive wizard warns about clear text (cli/prompt.ts:420); the flag path prints no warning; docs/cli.md:129 documents clear-text URLs for checks only.

In files mode, secrets-init passes PULSE_LOCATION to tokens.json unchecked, while PULSE_PROBE_LOCATIONS is checked (:175). A value with quotes gives `secrets-init: files mode done` and a JSON-escaped location in tokens.json. No injection, but the api has to refuse it.

No write is followed by fsync before its rename (cli/write-install.ts:292, scripts/secrets-init.mjs:87), so a power loss can leave an empty file. demo/init.mjs rewrites /shared/checks.json in place with writeFileSync; when docker compose up runs again on a running demo, the api can read a truncated file while it reloads. Not reproduced.
bun audit: 1 moderate advisory, minimatch@10.2.6 (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249). Dev dependency only, through eslint@10.13.0 of pulse-config; not in the CLI binary.

With --smtp-password-env or --webhook-secret-env, compose.yaml gets a bare key (`HOOK_SECRET:`), while docs/cli.md:171 says it gets a reference `${NAME}`. Compose fills the key from the shell or .env (`docker compose config` shows the .env value in notify's environment). So the secret is a container environment variable that any Docker user can read with docker inspect. The full setup passes its subscription SMTP password as a secrets-init file instead.

Status is published on all interfaces in full, dev and the CLI's full (*:8080; running stack HostIp ""). This is the intended public status page, listed in the port table. Console, api and mailpit are loopback only.
